package.title: Circuit encyclopedia
package.desc: Adds shared circuit-building guides to the encyclopedia.
glossary.entries.board.body.0: A circuit board expresses a rule with parts and wires. Connect inputs to parts, then connect the result to the output.
glossary.entries.board.body.1: Wires run from outputs to inputs. One output can feed several inputs, and each input reads one wire.
glossary.entries.board.title: Circuit board
glossary.entries.component.body.0: A component reads data at its inputs, computes according to its rule, and sends the result through its outputs.
glossary.entries.component.body.1: Place a component from the parts list or tray, then select it to inspect and adjust its settings.
glossary.entries.component.title: Components
glossary.entries.layout.body.0: On desktop, place parts from the parts list and drag between ports to wire them. Select a part or wire and press Delete to remove it.
glossary.entries.layout.body.1: Drag empty canvas space to pan, and use ⌘/Ctrl with scroll or pinch to zoom. Fit the canvas to see the full board.
glossary.entries.layout.body.2: On a phone, place parts from the tray and tap two ports to wire them. Tap a part to see its description and settings.
glossary.entries.layout.body.3: Both layouts edit the same circuit.
glossary.entries.layout.title: Desktop and phone
glossary.entries.parts.body.0: Some tasks unlock parts or part settings, or turn a completed circuit into a reusable part.
glossary.entries.parts.body.1: The tray lists the parts available for the current task. The component library records acquired parts and their descriptions.
glossary.entries.parts.title: Parts and the component library
glossary.entries.wiremode.body.0: On the phone’s circuit board, wires soon tangle once there are a few parts. The wire switch at the top right of the board cycles through three displays: “All wires”, “No input wires” (the wires leaving the input parts are not drawn) and “No wires”.
glossary.entries.wiremode.body.1: Hiding wires does not change the circuit. Each wired input has a small tag beside it naming the part it reads from, and while a dot is picked, the wires of its own part are still drawn.
glossary.entries.wiremode.body.2: The choice is remembered in this browser and stays the same from level to level.
glossary.entries.wiremode.title: Wire display
